</title>

<traits>

<column gap="tiny">

<row gap="medium">
**Price** 4 gp

**AC Bonus** +1

**Dex Cap** +4

**Check Penalty** -1

**Speed Penalty** —

**Strength** +0

**Bulk** 1

**Category** Light

**Group** Wood
</row>

---

Specialized crafters, often elves, create leaf weave out of sturdy leaves from ancient or magically enriched trees. Such leaves, when treated properly, have the strength of leather, and other tough plant materials hold the leaves together to form the armor. Such suits are popular among those who wish to avoid materials taken from slain beasts. As a material, leaf weave has the same [statistics](/Rules.aspx?ID=730) as thin wood.

<title level="2">Armor Specialization Effects</title>

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 275

Certain class features can grant you additional benefits with certain armors. This is called an armor specialization effect. The exact effect depends on which armor group your armor belongs to, as listed below. Only medium and heavy armors have armor specialization effects.

[Click here for the full rules on Armor Specialization Effects](/Rules.aspx?ID=211).

<document level="2" id="armor-group-7" />

<title level="2">Specific Magic Armor</title>

Armor Specialization Wood Source Treasure Vault pg. 9 Wood armor is generally flexible and light, but it can splinter as it breaks, throwing off shards and fragments that damage foes who deal you critical blows. If a foe critically hits you with a melee unarmed attack or critically hits you with any melee attack while adjacent to you, it takes piercing damage equal to 3 + the armor's potency rune value for medium armor, or 5 + the armor's potency rune value for heavy armor.
